### Observed differences

- In the earlier window the five activities A36, A37, A42, A43 and A44 ran in every trace (participation 100%, about one occurrence per trace); in the later window they run in only about 55 in 100 traces (about 0.55 occurrences per trace). They are still skipped together: pairs inside the group are absent from about 45 in 100 later traces. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL048, REL052, REL055]
- A27 shows the same pattern in mirror image: it ran in every earlier trace but in only about 46 in 100 later traces, and it now almost never co-occurs with the group (about 1 in 100 traces, versus every trace earlier). [OCC002, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037]
- Successors were rewired. Earlier, A25's outgoing transitions spread across the group (about 17–24 in 100 to each member) and each group activity sent about 17–25 in 100 of its transitions to A28; later, about 99 in 100 of A25's transitions go to A28, A26 has become the group's entry point (about 55 in 100 of A26's transitions, which earlier went to A27 in about 98 in 100), and the group's transitions now end in A31 (about 14–25 in 100 each) instead of A28. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- The order between A26 and the group flipped: earlier the group ran before A26 in about 98 in 100 joint appearances; later A26 runs before the group. A31, earlier always preceded by A27, now occurs without A27 in about 55 in 100 traces. [REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL043]
- Relative positions in the trace moved consistently: A28 earlier (mean 0.49 → 0.38), A26 earlier (0.62 → 0.53), the group later (about 0.41 → 0.57), A27 slightly earlier (0.65 → 0.60). [POS004, POS005, POS006, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]
- Close succession followed suit: A25–A36 and A42–A28 pairs within five steps nearly vanished (about 200 observed occurrences earlier, 1 later), while A26–A42 and A36–A31 appeared (1 earlier, about 107 later); these later pair profiles rest on very few observations. [LAG005, LAG016, LAG010, LAG013]
- Separately, the detour through A10 became rarer: A10 appears in about 13 in 100 later traces versus 32 in 100 earlier, and A15 routes to A10 in about 3 in 100 of its transitions versus 15 in 100 earlier; A10's later outgoing profile rests on only 26 transitions. [OCC001, DIR002, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment formed by A36, A37, A42, A43 and A44 was restructured. In the earlier window it was mandatory in every trace, running between A25 and A28 and followed by A26 → A27 → A31; in the later window A28 directly follows A25, and after A26 the process takes one of two mutually exclusive branches — A27 → A31 in about 45 in 100 traces, or the five-activity segment → A31 in about 55 in 100. The segment thus became optional (skipped in about 45 in 100 traces), moved from before A28/A26 to after A26, and changed its exit from A28 to A31; A27 now runs only when the segment is skipped. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]

Supporting signs: 106 evidence items qualified against about 1.2 expected for an unchanged process (all in the control-flow family), a gap far too large for sampling noise; the successor changes show the rewiring directly, the relation items show the order flip and the mutual exclusivity of A27 and the segment within jointly observed traces, and participation and position shifts agree with the same restructuring rather than with isolated fluctuations. [DIR003, DIR004, REL026, REL033, OCC002, POS006]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of pre-existing case types — for example a short path that was too rare to appear among the 200 earlier traces becoming frequent — rather than a newly introduced branch; the earlier window contains no trace without the segment or without A27, so such a variant would have been absent or extremely rare there. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]

Other differences: the A15 → A10 → A16 detour became rarer (A10 in about 13 in 100 later traces versus 32 earlier; A15 → A10 about 3 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions versus 15 earlier), with A10's later outgoing distribution based on few observations. [OCC001, DIR002, DIR001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 238 units tested, 106 items qualified, 1.18 expected without change. That's a massive excess — about 90 times the chance expectation. So this is not "insufficient evidence" by the screening comparison. The count is many times larger than expected.

All items are control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time (TWAIT) or resource (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND) items, so I must not discuss time or resources.

Now let me understand the behavioural story.

OCC items:
- OCC001: A10 participation 0.32 → 0.13 (32% → 13% of traces), mean occurrences 0.33 → 0.135. Support 64 → 26.
- OCC002: A27 participation 1.0 → 0.455 (100% → ~46%), mean 1.005 → 0.455. Support 200 → 91.
- OCC003: A36 participation 1.0 → 0.555. Support 200 → 111.
- OCC004: A37 participation 1.0 → 0.55. Support 200 → 110.
- OCC005: A42 participation 1.0 → 0.55. Support 200 → 110.
- OCC006: A43 participation 1.0 → 0.55. Support 200 → 110.
- OCC007: A44 participation 1.0 → 0.555. Support 200 → 111.

So a group of activities A36, A37, A42, A43, A44 (and A27) that occurred in every trace before now occur in only about 55% of traces (A27 ~46%). A10 dropped from 32% to 13%.

DIR items:
- DIR001 (A10): before, A10 → A16 in ~79% of outgoing transitions; after, A16 only ~38%, spread across many others. Support 66 → 26.
- DIR002 (A15): A15 → A16 84% → 94%; A15 → A10 15% → 3%. Support 347 → 345.
- DIR003 (A25): before, A25 → A36 24%, A43 22.5%, A44 18%, A42 17.5%, A37 17%; after, A25 → A28 98.5%. Support 200 → 201. This is a dramatic redirection: A25 now leads almost exclusively to A28.
- DIR004 (A26): before, A26 → A27 97.5%; after, A27 44.5%, A37 17%, A43 12%, A44 9.5%, A42 9%, A36 7%. Support 202 → 200.
- DIR005 (A27): A27 → A31 ~99.5% both windows. Support 200 → 91.
- DIR006 (A36): before A36 → A44 24%, A37 21%, A42 18%, A28 18%, A43 17%; after A36 → A31 25%, A42 22.5%, A44 16%, A43 17%, A37 16%, A28 gone. Support 202 → 111.
- DIR007 (A37): before A37 → A28 25%, A44 20%, A36 19%, A42 19%, A43 16%; after A37 → A36 26%, A44 23%, A31 15%, A43 21%, A42 12%; A28 gone. Support 202 → 111.

- DIR009 (A43): before A43 → A42 25%, A37 22%, A44 18%, A28 17%, A36 17%; after A43 → A36 25%, A42 22%, A44 19%, A31 14%, A28 1%. Support 202 → 110.
- DIR010 (A44): before A44 → A43 22%, A42 19%, A36 19%, A28 19%, A37 18%; after A44 → A42 25%, A31 21%, A43 20%, A36 19%, A37 14%; A28 gone. Support 203 → 111.

So A28 was a common successor of A25, A36, A37, A42, A43, A44 before; after, A28 is nearly gone as a successor, replaced by A31 (and A25 → A28 exclusively).

- POS001 (A15): mean position 0.167 → 0.179, slight shift later.
- POS002 (A16): mean 0.189 → 0.208, slightly later.
- POS003 (A25): mean 0.328 → 0.355, later.
